children: Evertz Technologies shares fell sharply Tuesday after the company reported lower first-quarter profit as higher costs offset a rise in revenue.

The Canadian software defined video network technology company late on Monday reported a decline in profit to C$7.96 million, or C$0.10 a share, for the three months ended July 31, down from C$11.9 million, or C$0.15 a share.
Analysts polled on FactSet expected a less precipitous decline to C$0.14 a share.
Expenses were higher in the quarter, from selling and administrative costs to research and development, as well as higher share-based compensation, all of which weighed on profit.
Gross margin also fell, reaching 58.6% compared with 61.4% in the same quarter last year.
The company also booked a foreign exchange loss of about C$531,000, compared with a gain of C$736,000 a year earlier.
Revenue rose in the period, however, to C$118.3 million, from C$112.1 million a year earlier.
At the end of August, the company said it had a purchase order backlog of more than C$259 million.
